campaign: Integrated validation, phase 2: bounded capability gains and evidence-gated simplification
doctrine:
overgo improves models, and itself, through its own inference and training, unattended. Every row closes or speeds up the improvement loop (measure, find the gap, train or change, judge on held-out data, promote or revert), or directly serves inference or training; otherwise it is not filed. The milestone is the loop itself (improvement-loop): from there, the scorecard's gaps generate the work. Progress is counted in promotions, not landings: a cycle that measured, trained or changed, judged on held-out data and moved main. While main trails the landings since its last promotion, rows that close the cycle rank above rows that only harden or slim it, and a cycle that cannot finish (killed, withheld) outranks every other row.

Finish partly landed rows before opening new ones. A consolidation reuses an existing owner and deletes the implementations it replaces in the same landing. A new shared component is allowed only when no existing owner can serve several real consumers, and it must remove more than it adds.

One meaningful run serves every obligation whose identity and contract match: it is written once, as one record with many readers. A run never judges what it produced, and a run leaves its evidence complete by its own contract (every protocol a suite's acceptance asks for), never half-written for a later landing to trip on.

The landing gate judges the commit; the improvement cycle judges the models. The gate's verdict depends only on the tree: unit, golden, hermetic-fixture and small-device checks. Suites that load real models, read the live store's evidence or sweep the device belong to the cycle, declared by build tag, and promotion of main requires them on the commit it promotes; a store write never changes a landing's verdict. A change's landing cost is read from its diff as three independent effects: the lanes it reaches, whether it expires the inference-surface guards, and whether it needs a pinned-media reconciliation. Lanes are the main cost, so false lane reach is cut. A surface move also expires every evaluation bound to the surface, so the re-evaluation it forces counts in its cost: surface changes are batched and land before an evaluation run, never between its runs, and the guards are re-acquired once after the last of them. A batch is one coherent change, normally one to three related rows, closed before it delays a user-facing result that is ready: an operating limit, not a gate. Dependency work is verified twice, separately: its build and test closure, and the guard surface, which stops at overgodb and runrecord. A saving is the net recurring cost removed, after the replacement tests and their maintenance. A check retires only when its replacement covers the check's actual acceptance contract, whether it moves to the cycle or is deleted; the landing scorecard reports and never refuses, so it replaces no check. The gate writes all numbers; messages name causes, effects and what disappears.

A step's verify fails before the change and passes after; a verify that already passes proves nothing, so a boundary is proved by the table row that fails today. Before a landing, what the gate refuses cheaply is run locally first: the claims check after any hand edit, the invariant tables, the rules' budget and exports, and the step's verify. A refusal found after the lanes costs an hour, and a retried landing rebuilds an identical gate binary.

Each row's rationale carries four plain lines: Serves (the loop stage, or the model or capability it runs or trains), Disappears (the owner reused, the implementations deleted, the tests retired or kept), Evidence (the run and record it reads or produces, and who else reads that record), Batch (the lanes its diff reaches, whether it expires the guards, and whether it needs a media reconciliation: three independent effects, each checked against the diff).

Landing speed is protected by observing it, not by a rule. Each structural boundary (a changed path's lanes, a package kept off the inference surface, a suite kept to the cycle) is pinned as an invariant row in one table per kind, never as a new test function or a snapshot of today's lists. At each periodic review the gate's measured lines in git log are read: the share of landings that reached no lane, lane minutes per landing, and executed versus cached package counts. A rise means a misplaced check or a new false reach, fixed by moving it and adding a table row. There are no time budgets or timeouts, no ratchet baselines, and no separate tracking subsystem.

Training research is measured at the lowest cost that answers the question, reusing what exists. Optimizer math stays on the device: host Muon on the tied embedding cost about 98 s a step, and moving it took a 540-step run from about 21 hours to 6 minutes. During training only scalars cross to the host (losses, norms, brake decisions), never weights or gradients per step. Reuse comes before acquiring: cached base losses keyed by the exact window plan, existing checkpoints, held-out sets and the verdict code, before any new dataset, pass or tool. An evaluation beats a training run, a norm beats a decomposition, and a one-time computation beats a per-step one. For a training rate question the order is: post-hoc tests on existing checkpoints, then the held-out brake from the training forward against cached base losses, then a per-layer relative step size, and per-direction spectral scaling last.

User-journey performance (owner, 2026-10-05). Optimize complete journeys, measured as action to usable result: submit to first visible answer, cold model selection to usable response, cancel to actual resource release, interrupted cycle to useful progress, with loading, admission wait, execution, publication and rendering kept apart. Start from the existing native benchmarks, allocation counts and CPU profiles of repeated reads, model loads, allocations and evidence reconstruction, and keep added instrumentation only when it explains a real elapsed-time gain. In the development loop one valid gate execution is shared by every compatible plan step and obligation, and validation and reuse are scoped by the actual dependencies (kernels, generated and embedded data, models, recipes, environment, subprocess effects); an unknown dependency keeps the broader coverage. A gain is judged against total maintenance cost (production code, tests, fixtures, instrumentation, gate work and upkeep): remove repeated processing through existing owners, and decline small gains that need disproportionate machinery. Prove with behavioral regression tests and comparable benchmarks, never a new performance ratchet, selector or framework.

items.title: Start the improvement cycle when what it measures has moved, not by hand

steps.title: Let the loop start a cycle when the measured surface moved since the last completed run, the obligations changed, or no actionable row is left, bounded by a count of such landings
steps.rationale: Serves: the cycle running when it can tell something, and never twice for one failure. Owner idea 2026-10-05 (start a run when result-affecting code changed since the last passing run, or the plan has no tasks left; no run while a commit uses the GPU for its longer test runs; a cap on the gap) with these refinements. (1) The surface is everything a cell executes, not only the inference outputs: the scorecard also judges throughput, first-output, load-time and peak-device-memory, so a speed-only change counts; take the inference surface, the training code, the kernels and the recipes, and the cycle's obligations digest (cycle_state.json already keys on it), because a new activation or dataset changes what a cycle measures without a commit. The computation-fingerprint step is the fine-grained form of the same test (per recipe and cell). (2) Compare with the last completed run of any outcome, not the last passing one: a failing cycle would otherwise restart itself while the surface still differs from the last pass; after a non-pass the failed measurement is filed as the next plan item and the loop waits for a change; the last passing run stays the baseline for promotion. (3) 'No tasks left' never happens while owner-blocked rows stay open: the condition is no actionable row (plan -next reports only blocked rows), or an explicit request. (4) The cap is a count of landings that touched the surface since the last run, with a derivation and a reason, not a bare number: the count at which bisecting a failed batch would cost more than a cycle; not elapsed time. (5) The trigger lives in cmd/loop's unattended driver (the 2 h limit is a property of the agent session's tool, not of the loop), never fires while a stop is active, and a killed run resumes at its first unpassed phase as today. Test first: with a recorded last run, a landing that touches the surface starts a cycle once, one that does not does not, a failed run is not restarted until the surface changes again, the cap starts a run, and an active stop starts nothing.

steps.title: Make a cycle take the same device turn the landings wait for, with timed cells starting only on a quiet machine
steps.rationale: Serves: no landing's device lanes overlapping a cycle's cells, and the cycle not starving landings. Evidence: the gate's retained lines show landings waiting 5 to 22 minutes for the shared device's turn (the landing's lanes have a turn wait, internal/landing/lanes.go:242, and the cycle holds its own lock, cmd/loop/improve.go:189, which refuses rather than waits); a cycle is about 2.5 hours of cells and lanes, and CPU-bound cells have read 2 to 13 times slower while a test ran beside them (hypothesis, to re-measure quiet). Change: the cycle takes the lane turn per phase, so device-lane landings queue behind a phase and not behind the whole cycle; the timed cells (media and serving first-output, throughput, load) start only when no landing is running and a landing's CPU-only lanes wait for them; quality cells may overlap CPU-only landings. Test first: a cycle phase and a landing's device lane never hold the turn together, and a landing that reaches no device lane is not delayed by a quality cell. Improvement cycle 15 (2026-10-05, measured at b69b2d98e, started 09:27, ended by the agent tool's 2 h limit at 11:27 in its models lane) ran beside twelve landings the owner asked for (plan, server and browser work with no device lane): the cells that finished while they ran read slower than cycle 14's on the CPU-bound and media cells (Krea-2-Turbo first output 14.0 to 19.7 s, LiveEdit video first output 42.9 to 58.5 s, granite-speech first output 3.0 to 3.9 s, Hy-Embodied training load 7 to 40 s, the dino embedding 4.4 to 5.2 s), while the inference first-output and throughput cells mostly moved by a few percent (Qwen3.5-9B throughput 77.6 to 71.4 tok/s the largest): consistent with the lesson that a build or test beside a timed cell slows it, a hypothesis to re-measure on a quiet machine, not a finding about the code; the Hy-Embodied training load (7 to 40 s, near LiveEdit's and Wan's 42 and 41 s) should be checked on its own. The lane phase also took longer than a landing would wait.

items.title: Cut the time a landing, a cycle and a resumed cycle cost, from the session's measurements

steps.title: Print what an interrupted cycle credited and the wall of each phase
steps.rationale: Journey inventory 2026-10-05 (read-only audit of what each journey already records; paths relative to the repository): interrupted cycle to useful progress, the least measured journey. The cycle prints no wall per phase and measurePhases (cmd/loop/improve.go:337-346) skips a credited phase silently, so nothing shows what was credited against redone; the only evidence is a unit test with a fake validator (improve_resume_test.go:17). Credit is all-or-nothing per phase (cycleState :233, written after a phase ends :339): the cells phase is credited only after every cell passes, selection re-runs every cell every cycle (cmd/validate/selection.go:107-111), a benchmark cell may take up to 6 h (validate/run.go:37) and a kill in cell 7 redoes cells 1 to 6; Fill has no credit at all. First step, trivial: print each phase's wall and what was credited. Test first: a resumed cycle's output names the credited phases and each phase's wall. The per-cell credit is sqa-defects/interrupted-credit and dev-speed/computation-fingerprint.

steps.title: Let one landing complete several plan steps with one gate run
steps.rationale: Serves: the landing wall, which is mostly lanes. Measured 2026-10-05 from the retained 'Measured by the gate' lines of the last 150 landings (go run ./tmp/gate_costs.go 150): the whole gate's median is 3m03s, its mean 8m and its p90 17m; lanes are 15.0 of 20.0 hours (75%), the test stage 3.8 hours (19%), and fix, vet, rules, invariants, verify and scorecard together under 1.3 hours. 16 landings reached no lane. The 14 whose lanes took 8 minutes or more ran the device lane (2.5 to 5 min), the cuda lane (5 min with all 16 packages executed and none cached, once 16 min) and the browser lane (54 s) one after another, and three also waited 5 to 22 minutes for the shared device's turn. Reaching a device lane is a real dependency (hostmath, loratrain and merges sit under device tests), so the saving is in sharing one lane run across steps and in overlapping what needs no device, not in narrower reach. A landing that reaches the device lanes costs 9 to 25 minutes however small, so several steps that all reach them should pay once: this session's seven audit landings cost about 1.5 hours of waiting. Share one valid gate execution across compatible plan steps and obligations. Change: -land takes more than one item/step, one commit with a Landed-Row trailer per step and each step's removal; every named step's verify must pass and the message states a Cause and a Predicted effect that covers them. Test first: two steps land together, both are removed, both trailers are in git, and one failing verify refuses the whole landing.

steps.title: Run the modeltest tests a landing's changed packages reach, in the landing
steps.rationale: Serves: failures found at landing time, not 2.5 hours later in a cycle. Evidence 2026-10-05: cycle 14's models lane found two bugs a landing could have (cmd/benchmark-report TestAcceptedSmallModelMMLUPro after smoke-declaration-recipe, and the cmd/validate accepted-coverage census after the E4B recipe replacement) because modeltest-tagged tests read the live store and only the cycle runs them. Change: the landing maps its changed packages to the tagged tests whose package closure (go list -deps -test -tags modeltest) contains one and runs those against the store; the four coverage tests took 83 s, so it runs only the reachable ones. Test first: a changed package inside a tagged test's closure selects it, one outside does not. Unknown dependencies (data files read at run time, subprocesses) keep the broader coverage; the selection is the package closure the toolchain reports, not a new selector or list.

steps.title: Profile the gate's own wall and overlap CPU-only lanes with the device lane
steps.rationale: Serves: the landing wall. The method that took a host LoRA step from 3m54s to 18.4 s (average cores = pprof samples over wall) applies to the gate: the device and cuda lanes run -p=1 and the machine has 32 cores. First measure, per stage and lane, wall and average cores for three real landings and record them in this step; then overlap the lanes that need no device with the device lane where nothing times a cell (a cycle's timed cells stay alone on the machine). Test first: the lane scheduler starts a CPU-only lane while a device lane runs and never two device lanes. Measured 2026-10-05 from the retained 'Measured by the gate' lines of the last 150 landings (go run ./tmp/gate_costs.go 150): the whole gate's median is 3m03s, its mean 8m and its p90 17m; lanes are 15.0 of 20.0 hours (75%), the test stage 3.8 hours (19%), and fix, vet, rules, invariants, verify and scorecard together under 1.3 hours. 16 landings reached no lane. The 14 whose lanes took 8 minutes or more ran the device lane (2.5 to 5 min), the cuda lane (5 min with all 16 packages executed and none cached, once 16 min) and the browser lane (54 s) one after another, and three also waited 5 to 22 minutes for the shared device's turn. Reaching a device lane is a real dependency (hostmath, loratrain and merges sit under device tests), so the saving is in sharing one lane run across steps and in overlapping what needs no device, not in narrower reach.

steps.title: Carry a measurement when the computation that produced it is unchanged
steps.rationale: Serves: the cycle (about 1.5 h of cells, 1 h of lanes and up to 1.9 h per bbh cell in the fill, 17 cells, re-acquired every cycle) and every resumed cycle. Most commits touch no inference path. Idea: a per-recipe computation fingerprint, the hash of the transitive Go packages that execute it (go list -deps), its kernels, recipe, weights and environment; a measurement taken at an equal fingerprint is carried (the replay-and-carry of evaluations already does this for quality, with a 32-case replay as the check), and only cells whose fingerprint moved run. First step of the work: measure over the last cycles how many re-measured cells had an equal fingerprint (record the count here), then the evaluation owner takes it. Replaces hand-listed runtime paths (the media pin was retired for that reason). Test first: an unrelated package change leaves the fingerprint, a package or kernel the recipe reaches changes it. Scope validation and reuse by the actual dependencies (kernels, generated or embedded data, models, recipes, environment and subprocess effects); a dependency the walk cannot see keeps the broader coverage rather than being assumed unchanged. Judge it against its total maintenance cost (code, tests, fixtures, gate work), and decline it if the measured count of re-measured cells with an equal fingerprint is small. Journey inventory 2026-10-05 (read-only audit of what each journey already records; paths relative to the repository): a cell's credit across an interrupted cycle is the same fingerprint question per cell (cmd/loop/improve.go:337-346, validate/selection.go:107-111). Improvement cycle 15 (2026-10-05, measured at b69b2d98e, started 09:27, ended by the agent tool's 2 h limit at 11:27 in its models lane): the lanes phase did not finish before the agent tool's 2 h limit, and a cycle resumes only at the commit it measured (credit is keyed by HEAD, the store and the obligations); twelve landings had moved HEAD by then, so the rerun the limit calls for would measure all 85 cells again (about 1.3 h) although no landing touched what any cell executes. Keying credit by what a cell executes (this step) is what lets a cycle survive the landings that run beside it.

items.title: Use checked evidence and explicit source and replay scope in reports

budget.reason: A carried held-out quality is attributed to the run that scored it: a bounded-by-identity walk of the carry chain through the receipt each run reports (the receipt read the evidence index already did, now one helper) and the scorecard cell's carried scope; the walk and the cell are the growth. Earlier allowance kept: the tolerant verdict visit, the recipe's gap record and its cell (the verdict-gap step).

steps.title: Carry a serving cell's environment so a changed environment reads Unknown, not changed
steps.rationale: Serves: a scorecard that does not call an environment change a regression or a gain. Audit 2026-10-05 (read): servingSummary.cell (internal/scorecard/scorecard.go:257-259,289-292) leaves Cell.Environment and CodeCommit empty although observation.Environment is set; Contract.Scope is the recipe alone (record.go:231-248, history.go:88-103), so observations from process/go and from cuda:0 for one recipe merge into one summary and Moves and scorecardMoves report 'changed' for a recipe-scoped serving change when only the environment changed. The model is not the gap: recipe.Definition.Model already makes the recipe model-specific. Failing test first: Moves on two serving cells with one Scope and different Environment is Unknown, today changed. Store observation.Environment and make holds treat a serving environment mismatch as Unknown. The held-out verdict cells have the same hole (internal/evaluation/heldout_verdict.go:398-404, producer read at scorecard.go:508): trace the held-out scoring run before changing them.

steps.title: Leave a transcription row's quality a gap, with its reason, when its report is unreadable
steps.rationale: Serves: the same robustness the verdict-gap step gave held-out verdicts. Audit 2026-10-05 (read): internal/scorecard/transcription_read.go:81-95,117-121 TranscriptionQualities returns an error that aborts scorecard.Build when one transcription report is unreadable; it should become a row gap with the reason, as heldoutRecord.unreadable does (the evidence stays strict: an unreadable report is never a value). Failing test first: an unreadable report leaves the other rows measured and its row's quality a gap that reads the reason. Correction 2026-10-05: the file is internal/evaluation/transcription_read.go, not internal/scorecard. SQA review of da1ec2c77 (docs/sqa_findings.json, 2026-10-05, source-based, nothing run) SQA-091 residual after d1fc1196a: VisitHeldoutVerdicts' unreadable callback loses the verdict identity (heldoutRecord keeps only a rendered reason) and heldoutRecords silently ignores a failed RequireServingObservation, so an unreadable observation reserves no recipe and surfaces no unknown; keep the original verdict or observation identity, a typed unreadable outcome and its binding scope; actual I/O and cancellation failures stay distinct from an unreadable record; a newer invalid same-recipe verdict is not replaced as current by an older one; keep strict nil-callback reconstruction. Test with the existing tiny fixture: mixed valid and invalid verdicts, newest invalid, missing observation.

steps.title: Join a baseline contract to its re-acquisition by comparison, not by suite family and label
steps.rationale: Serves: a baseline contract re-acquired as the protocol it was. Audit 2026-10-05 (read): cmd/validate/selection.go:166-168,224-245 and bound_records.go:71 match a baseline contract to a re-acquisition cell by ofFamily(Suite) plus the Prompting label, ignoring the Comparison (scorer, case set, execution) scorecard.Contract carries; two baseline contracts on one suite and label with different Comparison merge in compareContracts and bind replays only the newest record, so the other stays Unknown and promotion is withheld. This mostly arises from the environment in the Comparison (finding 1 of source-environment): resolve with it, after the owner's baseline-comparison-authority decision, or freeze the two-protocol case first (compareContracts is pure and table-testable).

steps.title: Attribute scorecard values to producing source, environment and protocol
steps.rationale:
Serves: honest candidate/main comparison and reuse from actual producer/input/effect facts. Disappears: publishing HEAD as producer, generic raw/reproducible defaults for missing provenance, suite-only protocol joins and recipe-only serving comparison when replaced by their actual existing owners. Evidence: existing acceptedRecords, typed Cell/Contract, result/run/receipt and bracket owners preserve record/model/input/scorer/execution/environment/protocol identities and alternatives. Keep publication source distinct from producer, full/current/carried scope explicit, independently sufficient mutable external-input acceptance and valid unchanged-input reuse. Unknowns keep visible values but cannot earn compatible evidence.
Current committed prerequisites: generic and specialized checked quality scope, native benchmark model/source/environment/workload/configuration qualification, strict same-producer training bracket pair IDs, and scorecard benchmark authority propagation are checked. Strict source/module scope is not cross-revision currency. b188 successful scalar/session/VQA Run content linkage is checked; it is not producing source/environment or fresh Operation. ce751528 terminal-run repairs failed/close-error handoff and refused publication through existing owners; required gate, exact media source chain and unchanged numerical/recovery/acceptance passed. Output identity and peak unchanged; single retained timing samples establish no causal gain.
Remaining: actual producing source/environment and scope-dependent currency for serving, checked held-out and benchmark evidence; full case/scorer/execution/protocol identity and alternatives through real reporting/reuse consumers. Workflow NewRun remains unbound; process/go is not device/peer producer environment. Actual execution Operation, partial phases/work/token denominators and missing capability producers remain connected to attempts. Freeze concrete incompatible-source/environment and two-protocol failing cases before adopting further policy; broad host verifier remains provisional, and unknown build/input/effect dependencies retain broader required coverage. Preserve recovery, cancellation/release on actual completion, authorization, numerical and fresh performance/artifact requirements. Batch true lane/test/guard/media reach; no manufactured metadata, new ledger, repeated full census or mandatory SQA gate. Count production/tests, evidence processing, analysis, instrumentation, gate and maintenance; profile before speculative kernels or large loader changes. Review findings 2026-10-04 (read, not yet measured on a toolchain change): (1) the evaluation Comparison binds the run's Environment id (internal/evaluation/plan.go:275), whose identity holds the host name and the Go runtime version (internal/runrecord/environment.go:56), so a toolchain bump or a host rename would make every baseline held-out cell Unknown and withhold promotion until the baseline moves: derive the comparison's environment from the device, backend and driver facts that change results, and keep host and runtime strings out of it, with a table row that fails today. (2) internal/evaluation/heldout_verdict.go:369-377: one held-out verdict that cannot be reconstructed aborts all of scorecard.Build; it should leave that row's quality as a gap with the reason. (3) A baseline published before comparison authority had no comparison on any evaluation cell, so the first cycle at new code is withheld by construction: it is handled once by moving main to the first record that carries them, never by relaxing holds. Finding 1 (the comparison binds the run's Environment id, whose identity holds the host name and the Go version, so a toolchain bump or a host rename would make every baseline held-out cell Unknown) waits for the owner's baseline-comparison-authority decision: re-keying the comparison identity now would make a record published at the current scheme, the one the decision proposes to promote, Unknown to every later candidate. Land it with a baseline published after the change, or in the same move of main. Finding 2 landed as the step verdict-gap (2026-10-05). SQA review of da1ec2c77 (docs/sqa_findings.json, 2026-10-05, source-based, nothing run): SQA-053 (P1) is this row's steps; SQA-078 (sampled replay acceptance and retained evidence scope explicit to consumers) and the unreadable-receipt residual of the carried-quality step (sqa-defects/carried-receipt) belong here too.

items.title: Carry what the GUI lane's review left: the continued adapter's baseline, cancellation, loop status load, copy command shell, surface

budget.reason: AddDelta (the row-at-a-time update) and LossAndGradsOf (the named gradients) are new; the update matrix, the weight-gradient transpose and the copy loop they replace are gone, and the step allocates 40 percent less

steps.title: The surface the first pass left: quantizeGGUF, the page's tone ternary, the byte order mark, the guard's expiry
steps.rationale: Left by the surface step and the review (2026-10-04): export.quantizeGGUF repeats cmd/gguf's quantize (open exclusive, quantize, sync, cleanup; they differ in importance handling, so one owner in internal/gguf, such as QuantizeToFile); the page's ok-or-caution ternary at six exact sites (a helper would not shorten them; skip unless a tone map is wanted); sampling/json_schema_ordered.go repeats the byte order mark dataset names; and the support tier's guarded rung never compares a guard's Surface with the current longform.Surface, so a guard that code changes expired still reads as held, which its detail text only warns of.

steps.title: Bind a continued adapter into its held-out verdict, or judge the baseline on the true base
steps.rationale: From the review (2026-10-04), still open: a run that continues an adapter (trainingworkflow.LoRA.From) judges its held-out verdict against the model as the prior adapter leaves it, which LoRA's own comment documents, but the verdict is bound to the base model (text_heldout.go, heldout_run.go) and the prior adapter's identity is recorded nowhere, so 'passed' reads as base to trained. Either bind the prior adapter's digest (peft's Adapter.digest, added with the merge plan) into the evidence the verdict publishes, with the recipe it names, or evaluate the baseline on the true base before the adapter is applied (Resume applies it at load). An evidence schema change; Resume also never compares adapter.Config.BaseModel to the model it is given. SQA review of da1ec2c77 (docs/sqa_findings.json, 2026-10-05, source-based, nothing run): SQA-092 (P2): LoRA.From loads a nonzero prior adapter, loratrain.Resume binds it before runHeldout predicts the baseline, and runHeldout publishes HeldoutTraining.Model as the base model id with no prior-adapter identity, so heldoutRecords can show a continued-adapter score as the unadapted base quality or as a base-to-trained comparison. Choose and document one authority: evaluate the true base before applying the prior adapter, or bind the prior adapter's digest, config and factors into the baseline's identity and report base plus adapter explicitly; thread it through recipe, run, verdict, reconstruction and scorecard; a label change alone or a fallback to an older base is not a fix; continuation and strict reconstruction stay. Review of the staged GUI lane merge (2026-10-05, three read-only reviews of the merged tree, nothing run) confirms it is still open: text_heldout.go:208-215 builds the trainer before the baseline is judged, and for a continued adapter (lora.go:79-83) loratrain.Resume binds and applies the prior adapter's delta into the model, so -lora-from prior reports baseline = base plus prior while the verdict binds only the base modelID (the comment at :209 says the opposite). Related (medium): -lora-from with -resume-run is not refused, and restoreRun (checkpoint_steps.go:191) freezes base plus prior as the base and adds the checkpoint adapter on top, counting the prior adapter twice.

steps.title: Keep conversations that share a prefix on one side of the held-out split
steps.rationale: From the verdict step (2026-10-04): conversationSplit gives every record its own group, so the variants of one chat (a prefix and its continuation, or near-duplicates the exact-text dedup keeps) can sit on both sides and the verdict reads memorization. Group by the conversation's opening turns (a digest of its first user message, or of the rendered text's first window) and assign groups, not records, to the held-out side by the digest order, through dataset.SplitOf with the records' groups. The source conversations are read by globbing a mutable directory (conversationFiles); the rendered dataset the run trains and judges on is content-addressed, so what was trained is identified truly, but its lineage to the source dataset is not recorded: record it (the rendered dataset derived from the source) when the split changes. decisions.question: The scorecard's serving cells (first-output, throughput, load-time, peak-device-memory) aggregate every attempt a recipe ever made: medians over all time, total tokens over total decode time, the highest peak ever. A landed improvement shows only as old samples are outnumbered and a peak never falls. Since delete-selection each cycle measures every serving cell once at the measured commit. Should those cells read the newest successful measured attempt instead, accepting one sample's timing noise in each cycle's moved list?

all-time aggregates
median of the newest few attempts
